messages:
zenith_ops: Hi team — we started seeing a deluge of 429s from our Dedicated pool (pool: polaris-prod-eu) around 09:12 UTC. Latency spikes to 3-4s for small requests too. Can you take a look?
kevin_support: Sorry about that — are those coming from the hosted API or your dedicated endpoint? any recent traffic changes? :eyes: 
zenith_ops: It's the dedicated endpoint: https://api.redwood.dev/v1/dedicated/polaris-prod-eu/generate. We kicked off a marketing campaign at 09:00, baseline qps ~180, peak bursts to ~1200 for 2min every 5min.
lisa_cs: tagging infra — @marco_oncall what does the pool look like? how many GPUs?
marco_oncall: pulling metrics now. polaris-prod-eu: 4xA10G (dedicated), autoscaler policy: target_util=0.75, cooldown=300s, max_nodes=6, min_nodes=2. Current nodes: 4.
kevin_support: can you paste the 429 response body or an example request id? helps trace.
zenith_ops: example request id: req_20260317_09_1187. 429 payload: {"error":"quota_exceeded","message":"pool capacity exceeded, retry later"} (this is from our app)
sre-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High 429 rate detected in polaris-prod-eu between 09:12-09:18 UTC. Avg token latency increased 2.8x.
marco_oncall: looking at node CPU/GPU util: GPU util jumped to 98% on node-3 during bursts, others ~85%. Autoscaler didn't add nodes fast enough because cooldown=300s and scaling is stepwise (one node at a time).
lisa_cs: so autoscaler lag + high per-node util = throttles. any noisy neighbor evidence?
marco_oncall: some indications: one workload (internal-rewrite) was sending long context requests frequently during bursts. KV cache miss rate also high which inflates per-request work.
kevin_support: can we get repro steps from zenith_ops for the burst pattern? timestamps, payload sizes, concurrency.
zenith_ops: sure: 1) burst every 5m starting 09:00 for 10s; 2) each burst ~600 concurrent connections; 3) avg input tokens 120, max 180; 4) used streaming mode.
kevin_support: thanks. immediate mitigation options: a) temporarily increase max_nodes to 8 or b) enable burst reserve (if available) or c) throttle at client side. Which do you want?
jenny_billing: note: increasing max_nodes will change billing and might incur burst overage. zenith_ops, want billing to approve?
zenith_ops: we want to avoid overage. any config we can change without extra nodes?
marco_oncall: short-term non-billing change: lower per-request concurrency by enabling queueing per-customer (max_inflight=50) or reduce target_util to 0.6 so autoscaler adds nodes earlier. But target_util change triggers gradual scale — cooldown still a factor.
kevin_support: we can also patch the autoscaler to allow multi-node scale-up when sustained util>90% across >30s. I can propose that to infra but it's not instant.
lisa_cs: can you provide the exact commands/logs we used to observe the issue? helps docs and postmortem.
marco_oncall: logs snippet:
```
[09:12:07] node-3 GPU util=98% (active sessions=612)
[09:12:09] autoscaler: evaluation -> add_node? false (cooldown active, last_scale=09:08:19)
[09:12:10] request req_20260317_09_1187 429 pool_overcapacity
```
kevin_support: good. Also noticed that the pool had quantization disabled for this model variant, making inference heavier. Could recommend enabling int8 profile for that model on this pool.
zenith_ops: is enabling int8 something we can toggle at runtime?
marco_oncall: yes, it's a config flip per model variant with a rolling restart of the runtime on each node (few seconds to drain). Low risk. Will reduce per-token latency/cost ~25%.
jenny_billing: reminder: quantization changes don't affect committed units but will reduce overage incurrence.
kevin_support: Proposed immediate plan (short-term): 1) set per-customer max_inflight=50 on polaris to smooth bursts (client-side queueing) 2) reduce target_util to 0.6 so autoscaler reacts earlier 3) enable int8 model variant for the model used by zenith (rolling) 4) temporarily bump max_nodes to 8 if still hitting 429s.
zenith_ops: do that. start with queueing + int8. Please avoid bumping nodes if possible.
marco_oncall: executing changes: setting max_inflight, toggling int8 on model:my-rewrite:v3 -> rolling restart initiated.
marco_oncall: int8 rollout complete on nodes 1-4. initial perf: per-request latency down ~18%, GPU util down ~12%.
kevin_support: can you monitor for next burst?
sre-bot: MONITOR: Next scheduled burst at 09:15 UTC.
[09:15-09:18] zenith_ops: observing fewer 429s, most requests succeed. latency around 1.2s now. Great. :tada:
marco_oncall: autoscaler still at 4 nodes, util peaked ~82% now and didn't trigger scale because target_util=0.75. I'll submit a change to lower to 0.6 for the next hour to be safe.
lisa_cs: please create a follow-up ticket to review autoscaler cooldown behavior and add option for immediate multi-node scale when multi-node util spike.
kevin_support: noted. zenith_ops — we'll keep monitoring and open an RFC for autoscaler improvements. Any post-incident asks?
zenith_ops: can you provide capacity planning guidance for our campaign cadence? want recommended pool sizing for baseline/peak.
kevin_support: sure — send expected baseline qps + peak qps pattern. Quick rule: aim for 60-70% mean GPU util at baseline and allow 20-30% headroom for bursts, or use burst reserve. We'll draft a calc.
marco_oncall: quick calc: current model cost per GPU ~ 120 qps baseline (with int8). For baseline 180 qps -> need 2 nodes; for bursts 1200 qps sustained -> need ~10 nodes. With autoscaler lag and cooldown, set max_nodes=10 and burst reserve or use client throttling.
jenny_billing: I'll prepare a pricing estimate for bumping to max_nodes=10 for campaign windows.
kevin_support: thanks everyone. Reopening if 429s return. We'll post a short postmortem and recommended config changes to docs. :white_check_mark:
zenith_ops: thanks team, much appreciated.
kevin_support: closing thread after we confirm stable for 2h.
